audit_question.question: When establishing F3 on leader entry, can recorded quorum support confined to inherited indexes advance the commitment object before reaching the first new-term index, including through voter-map replacement? The inspected construction and recalculation paths explain why such reports cannot cross the threshold.
audit_question.importance: Premature commitment advancement could make inherited entries eligible for application without the intended leader-term condition. The inspected mechanism addresses this bounded concern; it does not establish the validity of replication reports or overall application safety.
contexts: Leader entry with inherited log history and representable next index
Commitment recalculation following match reports or configuration replacement
Reports confined to indexes at or below the leader-entry last index
event_paths: Leader setup -> fresh commitment with startIndex = getLastIndex() + 1 -> initial no-op dispatch -> match reporting -> guarded recalculation
Voter-map replacement -> retained voter reports and zero-initialized new voters -> same guarded recalculation
counterevidence: The previously provisional fresh-object protection is directly supported by raft.go:455:576: runLeader invokes setupLeaderState, which constructs a new commitment with getLastIndex()+1. commitment.go:1:104 initializes commitIndex and voter reports to zero.

The threshold's intended meaning is explicitly documented in commitment.go:1:104: startIndex identifies the first index created in the leader term, whose majority replication is required before this leader marks entries committed. This is an attributed implementation contract, separate from the observed guard.

raft.go:455:576 dispatches a no-op before entering leaderLoop. raft.go:1244:1283 assigns dispatched entries incrementing indexes and the current term, then reports local match only after StoreLogs returns nil; storage failure requests follower state and returns without that report. This resolves the selected dispatch-ordering question for the shown leader-entry path.

commitment.go:1:104 shows both match and setConfiguration invoking recalculate under the mutex. Advancement requires quorumMatchIndex > commitIndex and quorumMatchIndex >= startIndex. Reports confined below startIndex therefore cannot advance this object.

setConfiguration preserves retained voter indexes, initializes newly included voters to zero, and leaves startIndex unchanged. Its recalculation cannot bypass the threshold, resolving the selected configuration-replacement concern.

Monotonic per-voter reports and mutex serialization, previously identified only from inventory, are visible in commitment.go:1:104. They supplement the threshold protection without independently establishing report truth.
unknowns: Remote report validity, disk agreement, crash durability, and association with the correct commitment object remain unverified; recorded support is not independently verified persistence.

The implementation of getLastIndex and reconstruction of inherited history are not supplied here. The explanation concerns the leader-entry index returned to the shown construction and dispatch paths.
Leader notification consumption and downstream application safety remain outside this establishment discriminator.
Index exhaustion and arithmetic wraparound are outside this bounded explanation; no repository contract for that boundary has been established.

The original normative-applicability uncertainty is narrowed by the explicit startIndex contract. Its satisfaction across all protocol histories, membership transitions, and recovery paths is not established by this review.
audit_question.trigger_rationale: Continue the selected F3 establishment lifecycle. Acquired construction, dispatch, and complete commitment code resolve the proposed inherited-support threshold bypass through an existing mechanism; no new candidate is selected.

selection_rationale: For the inspected leader-entry path, let L be the last index used to initialize the commitment and assume L+1 is representable. The threshold is L+1. Any recorded reports confined to inherited indexes at or below L yield a quorum index below that threshold, so recalculate cannot advance commitIndex. Configuration replacement retains the same threshold and uses the same guard. The initial no-op dispatch connects this threshold to newly assigned current-term work. This explains the bounded suspicion without deriving an obligation or claiming implementation correctness. All requested ranges were acquired; no deferred text is assumed. Remaining report-validity and recovery questions are explicit limitations rather than reasons to reopen this discriminator.
